problem: The sentence 'Field now rises by S, carriers hit velocity saturation, and the current grows only as S' attaches the wrong cause to the S factor. Current growing as S is the plain square-law result for fixed voltage (Cox rises as S, W/L unchanged). True velocity saturation makes the current grow slower than S, not exactly S, so a student learns a false link between velocity saturation and ID ∝ S.
fix: Field rises by S, and in the square-law model the current grows as S; in real short devices velocity saturation slows that growth further, which is why the numbers here are an upper bound.

where: Section 1, the Cox and kappa lines
problem: The symbols εox (permittivity of the oxide) and µn (electron mobility) are used without being defined, while P, C, VDD and f are defined in the formula block.
fix: Oxide capacitance per unit area is Cox = εox/tox, where εox is the permittivity of the oxide in farads per metre and tox is its thickness in metres. The parameter κ = µn·Cox·(W/L), where µn is the electron mobility in m²/(V·s), also multiplies by S.

problem: 'Every node you name — 28 nm, 7 nm — is described by these numbers' can be read as saying the node number equals the channel length. Modern node names are labels and no longer match L.
fix: Every node you name — 28 nm, 7 nm — carries a set of numbers like these, though the node name is a label and is no longer the actual channel length.
